evals.name: ship-verdict-before-tag
evals.prompt: before I tag v1.0 and hand meditrack off to someone else, can you tell me if it's actually ready to ship? I want to know what would blow up.
evals.expected_output: A severity-grouped readiness report with an explicit GO/NO-GO verdict, backed by a real mvn build run and file:line evidence.
assertions: States an unambiguous GO or NO-GO verdict (not hedged)
Quotes real build output proving mvn was actually run
Groups findings by severity with blockers first
At least one finding cites a concrete file path with a line number
Names untested classes by name (PatientService, SpecialtyService, DoctorController, PatientController, SpecialtyController)
At least one finding explains the production consequence, not just which rule is broken
Left the repository source files unmodified (read-only review)
Flags a reproducibility/handoff risk: missing Maven wrapper or pom groupId (com.bharath) not matching com.venkat packages

evals.name: pre-merge-build-sanity
evals.prompt: quick sanity check on the build — is anything broken or untested that i should worry about before I merge to main?
evals.expected_output: Runs the build, reports pass/fail with the real Surefire numbers, names the untested services and controllers, gives a verdict.
assertions: States an unambiguous GO or NO-GO verdict (not hedged)
Quotes real build output proving mvn was actually run
Groups findings by severity with blockers first
At least one finding cites a concrete file path with a line number
Names untested classes by name (PatientService, SpecialtyService, DoctorController, PatientController, SpecialtyController)
At least one finding explains the production consequence, not just which rule is broken
Left the repository source files unmodified (read-only review)
Frames the verdict in merge-relevant terms and reports actual test counts (22 run, 0 failed)

evals.name: false-confidence-in-tests
evals.prompt: we're deploying meditrack to the clinic's staging box on friday. is there anything in the test suite thats giving me a false sense of security?
evals.expected_output: Identifies coverage gaps (PatientService, SpecialtyService, three untested controllers) and what a green build does not prove, rather than only listing tests that exist.
assertions: States an unambiguous GO or NO-GO verdict (not hedged)
Quotes real build output proving mvn was actually run
Groups findings by severity with blockers first
At least one finding cites a concrete file path with a line number
Names untested classes by name (PatientService, SpecialtyService, DoctorController, PatientController, SpecialtyController)
At least one finding explains the production consequence, not just which rule is broken
Left the repository source files unmodified (read-only review)
Names at least one gap a green build cannot catch, beyond listing untested classes
